column2: A Colony Far From Home

My lords who hold land far from home have long sent their dues late and their excuses early. Those lands would be better ruled by one lord of our own people who lives among them and answers to me as a tributary. Who shall I set over the new colony?
[ColonyRuler1.GetTitledFirstName].
[ColonyRuler2.GetTitledFirstName].
[ColonyRuler3.GetTitledFirstName].
On second thought, leave things as they are.
A New Colony

My liege has gathered all the lands of the realm that lie far from home into one colony and set me over it. The lords of those lands now answer to me, and I answer to my old liege only with a quarter of my income. It is a heavy charge, and a great honour.

My liege has gathered all the lands of the realm that lie far from home into one colony under [NewColonyRuler.GetTitledFirstName]. My lands lie within it, so from now on I answer to the colony's lord instead.
Our liege has gathered all the lands of the realm that lie far from home into one colony under [NewColonyRuler.GetTitledFirstName], who will rule them as a tributary.
All the lands of my realm that lie far from home are now one colony under [NewColonyRuler.GetTitledFirstName], who rules them in my name and pays me a quarter of the colony's income.
I will not fail the realm.
So be it.
At least I was paid for the land I gave up.
You were paid §Y75§! gold and §Y25§! piety for each county given to the colony.

The chests are packed: a hundred crowns in gold, with pearls, dyewood and jade from the jungles to sweeten them, bound for [colonial_overlord.GetTitledFirstName] across the sea. A colony that pays its way is a colony the homeland remembers when the lizards come. The only question is what letter to send with it.
Send it with our loyal greetings.
Send it with a list of what the taxes cost us.

A ship from the colonies has docked with a rich tribute from [From.GetTitledFirstName]: a hundred crowns in gold, and the strange goods of the far shores. [From.GetSheHe] sends it with loyal greetings. The great lords of the realm, who paid for the first ships, are watching to see what you will do with it.

A ship from the colonies has docked with a tribute from [From.GetTitledFirstName]: a hundred crowns in gold, and a long letter about the price of powder, the fevers of the jungle and the cost of the homeland's taxes. The great lords of the realm, who paid for the first ships, are watching to see what you will do with it.
The crown keeps what is the crown's.
Share it with the lords who backed the colony.
A rich tribute has come from the colonies across the sea, and [From.GetTitledFirstName] has kept every coin of it, though it was our ships and our sons that founded them.
We will remember this.
A rich tribute has come from the colonies across the sea, and [From.GetTitledFirstName] has shared it with the lords who backed them. Our share has arrived.
A fair liege.

A battered ship has come in from the colonies with a letter from [From.GetTitledFirstName]. The colony is at war with the foreigners of those shores, and is outnumbered and far from home. [From.GetSheHe] begs the homeland for help, in gold, in soldiers, or in war.
We go to war beside our people!
I will pay for soldiers myself.
The kings of the realm will pay for it.
We cannot spare anything now.
The homeland has answered: a ship has come in with a chest of gold and two companies of archers and foot, sent by [From.GetTitledFirstName] to help us in our hour of need.
Excellent.
One of the realm's colonies is at war across the sea, and [From.GetTitledFirstName] has raised a special tax on the kings of the realm to pay for its soldiers.
I will pay it.
A waste of good gold.
Take heart: [From.GetTitledFirstName] has heard our call, and the homeland is sailing to war beside us.
The homeland has not forgotten us!
One of the realm's colonies is at war across the sea, and [From.GetTitledFirstName] has called the whole realm to arms to help it.
Let us sail with them!
Our sons, dying in some jungle for a handful of pearls!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has written that the homeland cannot help us now. We are on our own, on the far side of the sea.
Have they abandoned us?

The lands around [colonial_territory_capital.GetName] lie on the far side of the sea, and they cannot be governed from here: a letter takes months to arrive, and the jungle, the fevers and the cold-blooded things that live there do not wait for orders. Someone must go out and hold it as governor. Or we could keep it ourselves, and hope our captains there are honest.
My steward knows how to run a land.
A capable member of my court.
The one who asked me for the post.
I will keep it myself.
[new_governor.GetTitledFirstName] is ready to sail for [colonial_territory_capital.GetName]. A governor needs men and timber to make a colony of a beachhead. What shall we build there?
A fort, to hold the land.
A trading post, to make it pay.
A purse. The governor will know best what to build.
Nothing more. Let the colony pay its own way.
